item.title: 50 Years of Journal of Management Education: Developing Insights from the Archives
item.content:encoded:
The Journal of Management Education is celebrating its 50th anniversary with a special issue that invites scholars to develop insights from the journal's archives. This special issue seeks work that looks forward by looking back with a critical eye, examining how past scholarship can inform current and future directions in management education.

Appel publié par Organizational Behavior Teaching Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Critical examination of past research and scholarship in management education
  • Reflective analysis of how management education has evolved over the last 50 years
  • Lessons from historical research that inform current and future management education practice
  • Tracing the development of key themes, debates, and approaches in management education
  • Bridging historical insights with contemporary challenges in management education

item.title: Rethinking Business School Structures, Standards, and Success for Neuroinclusive Management Learning and Education
item.content:encoded:
Miriam Moeller, University of Queensland

Dana L. Ott, University of Otago

Matevž Rašković, University of Technology Auckland

Sophie Hennekam, Audencia Business School

Timothy J. Vogus, Vanderbilt University

Joy E. Beatty, Eastern Michigan University

Judith Clair, Boston College

With 15-20% of the global population neurodivergent and over half of Gen Z identifying as neurodivergent, business schools must examine how their systems serve diverse cognitive profiles. Rather than viewing neurodivergence as deficit requiring accommodation, this special issue foregrounds neurodiversity as natural cognitive variation that offers distinct strengths in learning environments.

This special issue invites contributions that reimagine management learning and education to serve neurodivergent learners, educators, and staff. Submissions should explore how neurodiversity challenges and enriches knowledge construction and group functioning in business schools, moving beyond workplace accommodation approaches and incorporating multiple theoretical perspectives and global contexts.

Appel publié par Academy of Management Learning and Education. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Neurodiversity in business education
  • Inclusive pedagogy and universal design for learning
  • Neuroinclusive curriculum design
  • Support systems for neurodivergent learners and staff
  • Assessment and participation norms
  • Intersectionality and neurodiversity
  • Double empathy problem in management education
  • Masking and disclosure in academic settings
  • Employability and career readiness of neurodivergent graduates
  • Organizational culture and ableism in business schools
  • Pedagogical innovations for neurodiverse learners
  • Academic and professional staff experiences with neurodivergence
  • Technology and AI for neurodivergent learners
  • Neurodiversity in non-WEIRD educational contexts
  • Social justice and diversity, equity, inclusion initiatives

Timeline

  • May 1, 2026: Optional virtual professional development workshop
  • May 13, 2026: Deadline for 3,000-word proposals for optional professional development workshop
  • November 1, 2026: Submission window opens
